writing-for-agents.note: Adapted: unslop pass over the prose, sharpened rule that a description is a trigger not a summary, SKILL-MECHANICS rewritten for astack's harnesses and sibling-path reach, including when the installer generates or validates Codex policy, unslop pointer and encode-lessons pruning rule added. Adds an astack-authored SOURCE-EDITS.md guide for locating installed skills' owning repositories and submitting approved source improvements through open-pr.

unslop.note: Rules verbatim; rule numbers are stable ids other skills cite. Description shortened to a human-facing line; disable-model-invocation set, from which the installer generates the Codex policy.

principles.note: All 23 principle skills as plain files under one user-invoked index. Frontmatter removed, applicability retained in the bodies, links adapted to local files, and unavailable skill references removed. Headings use sentence case and duplicate applicability statements are removed. Adaptations put migration preconditions before the rule, bound root-cause fixes to the task's scope, preserve external-constraint explanations, clarify boundary guarantees, and consolidate the mechanism hierarchy. Autonomy follows the user's authorization and approval preferences; context guidance follows writing-for-agents. Other edits correct the assertion-pattern heading, group failing-test and fix commits into one verified unit, allow reuse of a concrete tool, and narrow attack-the-premise to actor imbalances without treating an even census as proof. Earlier astack-added completion tests and one-off reply notes are removed. Upstream examples for pure functions, idempotency, and the reader-load/context-window cross-reference are retained. Minimize Reader Load links to Deep Modules, whose Matt Pocock provenance is recorded under codebase-design.

open-pr.note: Adapted under the global Pull Requests policy. Keeps narrow PRs, stack relationships, coherent commits, no-comments, technical-writing, unslop, title guidance, and default description sections. Cursor forge and deslop removed; Gitleaks hook install and T3 Code PR linking added. Links shared astack guidance for reusing and publishing PR test results, including delegated runs and the tested commit.

review-pr.note: Based on the pinned upstream directory, preserving the two axes, twelve Fowler smells, reviewer briefs, and separate reports. Adapts invocation metadata, removes Matt-specific setup, prioritizes user requirements, reviews the requested diff, records the PR head, and requires attributed posting of actionable findings through harden-pr's shared PR helper. Removes the old rubric and prompt builder. Links shared astack guidance for reusing and publishing PR test results, including delegated runs and the tested commit. Posts only actionable findings, keeps summaries in the conversation, and puts test results in the PR description.

technical-writing.note: Verbatim apart from a shorter description, the unslop pointer as a sibling link, and one pstack-specific formatting line removed.

no-comments.note: The Comment Sicko subagent is gone; its keep list and flag rules are the skill body, applied by the agent itself. The /how, /why, and /architect calls became read-the-history and sketch-the-shape instructions; principle references point at ../principles files.

harden-pr.license: MIT, kept in skills/harden-pr/LICENSE-pstack, LICENSE-mattpocock, and LICENSE-gstack
harden-pr.note: Adapted from the pinned gstack review directory. Retains core checks, specialist criteria, independent adversarial review, and outside structured review. Consolidates scope and dispatch, removes numerical scoring and aesthetic rules, and replaces gstack runtime dependencies. Adds astack PR posting, requested follow-through, and targeted mutation guidance. See upstream/review-adaptations.md. Links shared astack guidance for reusing and publishing PR test results, including delegated runs and the tested commit. Posts only actionable findings, keeps summaries in the conversation, and puts test results in the PR description.

grilling.note: Preserves the design-tree interview, frontier rounds, recommendations, and shared-understanding checkpoint. Removes decorative emoji from the question template. Makes invocation explicit with matching Codex policy and a human-facing description. Allows direct factual lookups and delegates independent exploration that can run alongside the interview.

improve-codebase-architecture.note: Preserves exploration, visual candidate reports, user selection, grilling, domain-model updates, and optional interface alternatives. Uses local skill links, tolerates absent project documentation, and adds targeted astack principle references. Reports use t3-preview, inline assets, dark styling, and plain candidate sections. Reads the Deep Modules principle and permits boundary terminology. DEEPENING.md and DESIGN-IT-TWICE.md are tracked under codebase-design, their upstream source. Consolidates report instructions in HTML-REPORT.md and glossary/ADR actions in domain-modeling. Reads principles at the relevant decisions and applies the deletion test from Deep Modules instead of restating it. Passes identified glossary and ADR locations to domain-modeling. The report links to DEEPENING.md for dependency classification.

domain-modeling.note: Preserves glossary updates, multiple contexts, and selective ADR creation with both format references. Uses sentence-case headings and reference-style links in the sample context map so example repository paths are not treated as installed skill dependencies. Consolidates glossary locations and format in CONTEXT-FORMAT.md and ADR locations, numbering, and examples in ADR-FORMAT.md. Keeps ADR eligibility and lazy document creation in SKILL.md; removes repeated criteria and directory trees. Makes invocation explicit with matching Codex policy and a human-facing description. Uses glossary and ADR locations identified by the caller or project instructions, retaining upstream defaults otherwise.

codebase-design.license: MIT, copied from repository-root LICENSE to skills/principles/LICENSE-mattpocock and skills/improve-codebase-architecture/LICENSE-mattpocock
codebase-design.note: The shared reference is now the Deep Modules principle; its workflows live under improve-codebase-architecture. Removes skill frontmatter and the separate Codex display metadata, adds an applicability trigger, and uses sentence-case headings. Consolidates Relationships into the glossary and repeated seam definitions into the principle. Removes the blanket restriction on boundary terminology. Pure-function and assertion guidance point to Boundary Discipline and Test Behavior, Not Implementation. Interface exploration reads Exhaust the Design Space and passes applicable caller principles to designers. Old tests are removed only after their behavior is covered at the new interface. Designer briefs include project domain vocabulary when available. Replaces the claim that fewer methods require fewer tests with guidance on simplifying test setup.

worktree-cleanup.note: Adapted for model invocation on cleanup, resource audits, and lane closeout. Checks unfinished work first and reports blockers before cleanup or handoff writes. Uses Git inventory, T3 thread ownership, and task resource evidence instead of Cursor-specific auditing. Covers processes, Docker storage, disposable test databases, and t3-preview HTML and quick tunnels. Preserves shared resources and the daily-driver T3 connection. Adds preview ownership records; simulator and cache cleanup remains optional. Prose trimmed to task-specific rules and teardown hazards.

ship-pr.note: Adapted as ship-pr, a model-invoked entry point for landing an existing PR or stack. Reuses the shared PR follow-through procedure and existing review evidence. Removes the mandatory independent verification pass and separate verdict protocol; refreshes verification when evidence is missing or changes invalidate it. Retains safeguards against merging unverified head changes.

how.license: MIT, copied from pstack/LICENSE to skills/how/LICENSE
how.note: Preserves the upstream opening directive, simple and complex delegation paths, separate explorer and explainer prompts, and explanation structure. Shortens the description to the 200-character cap. Replaces Cursor Task parameters and fixed models with available subagent tools and a read-only direct fallback. Uses portable file-search instructions, validated reference links, and sentence-case headings. Makes explorer findings conditional in the explainer prompt so the direct-explain path works.

why.license: MIT, copied from pstack/LICENSE to skills/why/LICENSE
why.note: Preserves the upstream investigation workflow, default parallel source sweep, confidence framework, separate investigator and synthesizer prompts, and all source playbooks. Shortens the description, adapts tool discovery and delegation to the active harness, permits explicitly scoped investigations, and reports unavailable sources as gaps. Treats provider tools and warehouse schemas as examples to verify. Uses validated links and sentence-case headings.

teach.license: MIT, copied from pstack/LICENSE to skills/teach/LICENSE
teach.note: Preserves the upstream teaching directive, five-step conversational workflow, progressive diagrams, and concrete examples. Shortens the description, reads how and why by sibling paths, scopes investigation before dispatch, and returns findings for a single teaching explanation. Adapts image generation to available tools and the user's requested colors. Links the existing unslop skill.

reflect.license: MIT, copied from pstack/LICENSE to skills/reflect/LICENSE
reflect.note: Preserves the upstream three review lenses, separate reviewer and synthesizer prompts, durable-learning criteria, and selected-edit workflow. Adapts transcript discovery and delegation to the active harness with direct fallbacks. Removes the finding quota, limits missed-trigger tuning to model-invoked skills, and files backlog issues only when requested. Routes authoring through writing-for-agents, shared lessons to principles, and approved astack improvements through the source-editing PR workflow. Honors prior edit authorization. Updates the synthesizer's trigger examples for astack metadata.

create-verification-skill.license: MIT, copied from pstack/LICENSE to skills/create-verification-skill/LICENSE
create-verification-skill.note: Preserves the upstream creation workflow, complete feature-map examples, and maintenance procedure under one entry point. Shortens the description and replaces Cursor-only paths with project skill conventions. Adds shared authoring guidance and conditional verification, automation, idempotency, and testing principle links. Adapts delegation with a direct fallback, respects startup scope and isolation, reports unreachable features as unverified, and opens maintenance PRs when requested. Splits the maintenance live-pass paragraph so its health, evidence, and cleanup requirements are readable.

architect.note: Starts from the pinned pstack directory, retaining the five phases, candidate brief, design red flags, and rationale template. Replaces arena and fixed models with available subagent tools, links local principles and exploration skills, preserves design-only scope, and requires the local UI selection workflow. Applies no-comments to sketch guidance. See upstream/implementation-adaptations.md.

implement.license: MIT, kept in skills/implement/LICENSE-pstack and skills/implement/LICENSE-mattpocock
implement.note: Uses the pstack Feature playbook as the base, retaining design ownership, the four-part throughput checkpoint, implementation delegation, diff review, and verified units. Incorporates Matt implement guidance for TDD, regular typechecking and focused tests, final review, and commits. Adapts provider-specific dispatch, local skill references, and task-scoped delivery. Retains Matt Codex metadata. See upstream/implementation-adaptations.md. Multi-phase execution follows the shared orchestrate/STATE.md convention; delegated workers return receipts to the sole state writer.

tdd.license: MIT, kept in skills/tdd/LICENSE-pstack and skills/tdd/LICENSE-mattpocock
tdd.note: Keeps Matt SKILL.md, tests.md, mocking.md, and Codex metadata, plus pstack regression workflow as BUG-FIX.md without skill frontmatter. Reuses established testing boundaries, links the existing testing principle and Deep Modules, and explicitly permits concrete refactoring after green. Removes narration comments from code examples under no-comments. See upstream/implementation-adaptations.md.

to-spec.note: Retains the upstream process, inline spec template, decision lists, prototype exception, and Codex metadata. Replaces setup and fixed tracker labels with the agreed destination, reuses settled testing boundaries, scales user stories to the feature, and records blocking questions. See upstream/implementation-adaptations.md.

prototype.license: MIT, kept in skills/prototype/LICENSE-pstack and skills/prototype/LICENSE-mattpocock
prototype.note: Starts from Matt prototype directory and retains logic scenarios, state display, UI alternative criteria, and switcher behavior. Uses pstack scratch isolation and matching-surface verification. Adapts real-route edits to static HTML mocks, local visual constraints and t3-preview, with selection before real components and scoped production handoff. Retains Codex metadata. See upstream/implementation-adaptations.md.

diagnosing-bugs.note: Retains the upstream six phases, feedback-loop menu, minimization criteria, prediction format, checklists, human-loop script, and Codex metadata. Links shared testing and root-cause guidance, preserves diagnosis-only scope and provisional investigation without reproduction, qualifies flake-rate claims, and treats hypothesis count as guidance. Removes narration comments from the shell template under no-comments. See upstream/implementation-adaptations.md.

implementation-slicing.note: Only vertical-slice and blocking-dependency guidance is retained in the existing Sequence Verifiable Units principle. No standalone to-tickets skill, tracker workflow, or ticket templates are installed. The rest of the principle retains its pstack provenance under principles.

wizard.note: Retains the upstream process, Bash template, example stage, and Codex metadata. Makes invocation explicit with a human-facing description and matching Codex policy, reuses agreed scope instead of requiring repeated confirmation, and limits CI and local writes to their agreed destinations. Adds secret redaction guidance and documents the literal single-line dotenv subset. The template preserves input whitespace, stops on EOF, quotes supported dotenv values, decodes existing quotes without evaluation, and rejects unsupported syntax before writes. Removes narration and decorative comments while retaining public helper contracts and the stage marker. Offline tests cover reruns, captured secret payloads, EOF, unsupported values, and action-only stages.

orchestrate.note: Preserves coordinator roles, brief, pilot and rolling execution, completion queue, stack ownership, SHA-keyed verification, failure handling, and escalation. Replaces Cursor, cloud, Graphite, and Bun runtime dependencies with available tools and an astack-authored STATE.md procedure. Honors execution and merge authorization separately and routes merges through ship-pr. See upstream/planning-adaptations.md. Shares its core state, checkpoint, and resume convention with multi-phase-plan and sequential implement sessions.

multi-phase-plan.note: Preserves the ordered plan skeleton and per-PR evidence workflow. Replaces provider-specific execution, scheduling, control, and model dependencies with astack skills and available tools. Scales live scenarios to risk, allows reasoned performance exemptions, and follows existing human gates. Ports the checker to Python standard library. See upstream/planning-adaptations.md. Records one execution store reused by implement and orchestrate, including durable handoffs and resume reconciliation.

wayfinder.note: Preserves the map, decision tickets, ticket types, fog of war, and chart/work modes. Adapts tool invocation and skill links, local tracker fallback, concurrent session claims, cancellation and supersession, user-authorized execution, and explicit continuation. Retains Codex metadata. The local tracker reference retains only wayfinding operations and relevant shared conventions. See upstream/planning-adaptations.md.
